specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX (Arrow Lake-HX, 20c/20t: 8P + 12E, up to 5.2 GHz)
specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (Advanced Optimus)
specs.storage_type: NVMe Gen4/Gen5 M.2 (2 slots, PCIe5 main)

battery.notes: 83Wh. NBC same chassis: WiFi 5h50 (275HX); 255HX + 5070 draw less, users report ~3.5-4.5h mixed on lower tiers.

price.notes: BB regular $2,799.95 verified 2026-11-24 (sku 19320070). BBY customer pool 4.09/5, n=64.

offers.name: HP OMEN MAX 16 16" 165Hz Gaming Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX - 32GB DDR5 - 1TB SSD - RTX 5070 - Windows 11 Home - Shadow Black

reviews.quote: Lesser SKUs of this model start with the Core Ultra 7 255HX CPU and RTX 5070 Ti GPU with a 2K IPS display for $2500 USD.
The HP Omen Max 16 offers good performance, stunning visuals and layered sound, but it's a lot to lug around.

praises: Best price/perf of the Max line: full OMEN Max chassis, 32GB and RTX 5070 under $2,800 CAD (BBY pool 4.09/5, n=64)
'Beautiful laptop with an all metal chassis extremely powerfull plays all my games at max settings while staying quiet' (BBY, line-wide)
Matte 165Hz IPS avoids the glossy-panel reflections owners complain about on the OLED tiers (BBY)
RAM upgradeable — 'besides the battery and SSD, the RAM can also be upgraded... several levels above many other laptops that have soldered RAM' (BBY)
255HX runs cooler than the 275HX tiers, so Balanced mode stays quieter in everyday gaming (BBY 'staying quiet' reports)
complaints: 8GB VRAM on the RTX 5070 is the tightest of the line for 1440p ultra textures and local AI — pair with DLSS
Battery still only ~4h unplugged: users peg the line at 3-3.5h on heavier tiers (BBY)
165Hz IPS panel is the baseline of the line — no HDR, visible backlight bleed vs OLED siblings
Still 2.81 kg + ~2 lb brick — no portability discount for the cheaper tiers (Tom's: 'a lot to lug around')
Fan ramps are loud in Performance/Unleashed modes (up to ~55-61 dB(A) per NBC on the same cooler)

design_philosophy: The entry-to-mid price point of the OMEN Max line: NBC explicitly describes the lesser SKUs as 'Core Ultra 7 255HX CPU... with a 2K IPS display for $2500 USD' — this CA config is exactly that philosophy: keep the big Arrow Lake-HX chassis, 32GB and dual upgrade slots, and trim spend into the 165Hz IPS panel and a cooler 20-core 255HX.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the NBC/Tom's reviewed 5090/275HX OLED config (see SHARED-omen-max16.md). Deltas: GPU 5090→5070 = gaming −3.0, ai_ml −2.0 (24→8GB); CPU 275HX→255HX = productivity −0.5, thermals_noise +1.0 total (cooler 20-core part, less all-core throttling), battery +1.0; panel OLED→165Hz IPS = screen_quality −2.0, readability_dark −1.0 (bleed vs OLED blacks), readability_bright +0.5 (matte), creative_work −1.0 (no OLED HDR/contrast).
